division.heading: Lawyers’ Charges, Retainer Agreements and Right of Review

operative_text.controlling:
10.19(1)  A review of a lawyer’s charges must take into
consideration the factors described in rule 10.2, except to the extent
that a retainer agreement otherwise provides.
(2)  A review of a retainer agreement must be based on the
circumstances that existed when the retainer agreement was entered
into.
(3)  The review officer may, in a review of a lawyer’s charges,
allow the charges, or vary, reduce or disallow all or any of the
charges, and certify the amount payable for and against each party,
and may issue an interim certificate.
(4)  A review officer’s decision must be given by an interim or
final certificate, which may be endorsed on a copy of the lawyer’s
account, and the certificate must
(a) certify the amount to be paid by each party or person,
(b) certify any special circumstance and the amount to be paid
by each party or person with respect to the special
circumstance, and
(c) be dated and signed by the review officer.
(5)   An interim or final certificate of a review officer that meets the
requirements set out in subrule (4) is conclusive proof of the
amount that a party or person who had notice of the review must
pay.

BOOK_A.title: Review Ofﬁcer’s Decision
BOOK_A.commentary:
See also R.10.9 n.
The appellant had argued for a decision on whether the Review Ofﬁcer found the 10 lawyers’
periodic bills being reviewed were interim and to be reviewed as a whole at the end, or each
ﬁnal and to be reviewed individually. The parties disagreed on that topic. The Review Ofﬁcer
never decided that basic question, and his view is unclear, which omission was a clear error of
law.¹
It is vital to determine that question for two reasons: to know how to assess each bill, and
to see whether any bills were being reviewed outside the one-year limitation (and most of these
bills were reviewed more than a year after their receipt under R.10.10(2) ).²
So the decision was
quashed and a new review by a different Review Ofﬁcer was ordered.³
If a review ofﬁcer ﬁnds the retainer agreement unfair, or if a King's Bench judge or the Court
of Appeal ﬁnds the decision under appeal unreasonable, then that higher ofﬁcer or judge must
analyze the fee afresh, and set the fee on any reasonable basis, not necessarily a percentage of
recovery.⁴
If a lawyer collects fees from a retainer and then his or her account is reduced on review, that is
res judicata and a court order. The same is true if the account is reduced on appeal from review.⁵
A duty to refund is implicit when a paid lawyer’s account is assessed down.⁶
One common-law spouse was in privity with the other and bound by adverse court rulings
against the other, though not named in the style of cause.⁷
On negligence by the lawyer, see R.10.1 and commentary, supra.
Because of Rr.10.2 and 10.19, even an unenforceable contingent-fee agreement has some
(limited) relevance.⁸

BOOK_A.operative_text_note: Book A's rule text (lines 1635-1652, title on line 1634) has the same words as the official text (compared by hand, subrules (1)-(5) and paragraphs (4)(a)-(c)) with one addition: the bracket label '[Payment for lawyer's services and contents of lawyer's account]' after 'rule 10.2' in (1) (the official text has no label; the official title of 10.2 reads 'Payment for lawyer's services and contents of lawyer's account', and Book A's label in 10.18(4) reads 'contents of a lawyer's account'); it also differs in ligatures ('ofﬁcer', 'certiﬁcate'), spacing and line breaks, and in (3) it prints 'the charges and certify' where the official text has a comma ('the charges, and certify'). It has no amendment bracket (the official history is 'AR 124/2010', no amending regulation). The official text controls; the raw Book A lines are not kept.
BOOK_A.commentary_review_flag: Read in full, p.10-34 (line 1634) to p.10-35 (line 1696): title (line 1634), rule text (lines 1635-1652), Related Provisions (lines 1671-1672, '10.9 (contingency fee agreement reviewable for reasonableness).'), and the note (lines 1674-1695; page marker 10-35 line 1668) with its footnotes: p.10-35 fns 1-8 (block after the text of 10.20, line 1705 ff.) = 8; the p.10-34 footnote block (line 1654 ff.) holds fns 1-6 of the 10.18 note. Read against the official text: the rule text equals official 10.19(1)-(5) apart from the bracket label; the Related Provisions label '10.9 (contingency fee agreement reviewable for reasonableness).' is a label for official 10.9 (title 'Reasonableness of retainer agreements and charges subject to review', line 1490; 10.9 covers retainer agreements and lawyer's charges generally, not only contingency fee agreements, as the 10.9 flags note); its closing full stop is printed as is. 'See also R.10.9 n.' lands. Statements that are case-law summaries and not the rule: the appeal about whether the ten periodic bills were interim or final and the Review Officer's failure to decide (Larocque v. Kantor LLP 2024 ABKB 327, fns 1-3, paras 10, 14, 18, 23-24, 26, 1, 18, 20-22, 24, 26, 28; the same decision is cited in the 10.10 note, p.10-25 fn 7); 'most of these bills were reviewed more than a year after their receipt under R.10.10(2)' agrees with official 10.10(2) (one year, since AR 36/2020); the fee analysed afresh 'on any reasonable basis, not necessarily a percentage of recovery' (fn 4 Tallcree F. N. v. Rath & Co. 2022 ABCA 174, paras 90, 107-08, 110); 'that is res judicata and a court order' and 'A duty to refund is implicit when a paid lawyer's account is assessed down' (fns 5-6 Severin v. Veale (#2) 2000 ABCA 180; Hanke v. Resurfice Corp. (#2) 2006 ABCA 116; official 10.21 lets the Court order repayment on the client's application); privity between common-law spouses (fn 7 Polis v. Edwards 2010 ABCA 59, paras 25-37); 'Because of Rr.10.2 and 10.19, even an unenforceable contingent-fee agreement has some (limited) relevance' (fn 8 Betser-Zilevitch v. Prowse Chowne 2021 ABCA 129, paras 19-21; official 10.19(1) makes the 10.2 factors apply to a review of charges 'except to the extent that a retainer agreement otherwise provides'). FLAG: 'On negligence by the lawyer, see R.10.1 and commentary, supra.'
